sub: Named after al-māʿūn, “small acts of help”, the surah’s last word
theme: Shows what happens to character when a person stops believing in the Judgement: he pushes the orphan away, ignores the poor, neglects prayer, shows off, and refuses even small favours.
story: Reports differ on whether it was revealed in Makkah or Madinah. Ayat 1–3 describe someone who openly denies the Judgement; ayat 4–7 describe people who pray, but carelessly and for show, which fits the hypocrites.

Reports also differ on whom it first described: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū Jahl, a hypocrite, or others. One report says a wealthy man struck an orphan with his stick when the orphan asked him for something.
The message runs through both parts: belief in the Hereafter shapes behaviour. Without it, a person feels no duty to the weak and no sincerity in worship.

sections.title: The one who denies the Judgement
sections.meaning: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? He is the one who shoves the orphan away and does not urge anyone to feed the poor. His denial shows in how he treats the weak.
points: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?
He pushes the orphan away roughly
He doesn’t urge feeding the poor
sections.matters: It ties belief to behaviour. Someone who expects no reward and fears no punishment has no reason to be kind to the helpless, and it shows in how he treats them.
sections.story: Reports differ on whom it describes: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū Jahl or a hypocrite. One says a man who slaughtered a camel every week hit an orphan with his stick for asking him for something.
explained: Ad-dīn here is the Recompense: the reckoning and reward of the Hereafter. The one who denies it yaduʿʿu al-yatīm: he pushes the orphan away harshly, keeps him from his rights and shows him no mercy, because his heart is hard and he hopes for no reward.

He does not even urge others to feed the miskīn, the poor person with nothing, so he certainly does not feed him himself. The blame falls on those who could help and hold back out of stinginess, not on those truly unable.
teaches: What you believe about the Hereafter shows in how you treat the weak.
Honour orphans and protect their rights.
Feed the poor, and encourage others to feed them too.
sections.hook: The surah opens with a question, araʾayta, “have you seen…?”. Fa-dhālika, “that is the one”, answers with two actions: pushing the orphan (2), not urging food for the poor (3).

sections.title: Woe to those careless in prayer
sections.meaning: Woe to people who pray yet are heedless of their prayer: delaying it, neglecting it, not caring whether they pray. They do good only to be seen, and they refuse even the smallest help to others.
points: Woe to those who pray but are heedless of it
They pray and do good to be seen
sections.matters: The first part showed a heart with no mercy for people. This part shows the same emptiness in worship: prayer without sincerity, and wealth held back from others. Neglecting Allah’s rights and people’s rights go together.
sections.story: No specific incident is named for these ayat. They describe hypocrites, who prayed in public when people could see them and left prayer when alone.
explained: The wording is ʿan ṣalātihim sāhūn: heedless of their prayer, not “in” it. Forgetting something during prayer happens to everyone, even the Prophet ﷺ. The blame is for neglecting prayer itself: missing its time, skipping its parts, or not caring whether one prays at all.

Yurāʾūn: they do their deeds to be seen. Doing a deed for Allah and being pleased when people find out is not showing off. Al-māʿūn: small things neighbours lend, like a bucket, pot or axe; others say it means zakah. If they refuse even small things, what about more?
teaches: Pray on time and with care; neglecting prayer is serious.
Do good for Allah, not for an audience.
Lend and share everyday things freely.
Pay the zakah you owe; withholding it is a grave wrong.
sections.hook: Fa-wayl (4) turns from the denier to people who pray. Three descriptions follow: sāhūn (5), yurāʾūn (6), yamnaʿūna al-māʿūn (7). The surah’s name is its very last word.

groups.text: Have you seen the one who denies the Judgement and its reward?
He pushes the orphan away and doesn’t urge anyone to feed the poor.
Woe to those who pray but neglect their prayer.
They pray to be seen and refuse even small acts of help.

1.explain: Araʾayta: have you seen, do you know him? Yukadhdhibu bid-dīn: he denies the Recompense, the resurrection and reckoning, so he does not believe what the messengers brought.
1.why: Reports differ: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū Jahl, ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾidh or a hypocrite. One says a man who slaughtered a camel every week struck an orphan who asked him for something.

2.explain: Yaduʿʿu: shoves away roughly. He oppresses the orphan, keeps him from his rights, and shows him no kindness, because his heart is hard and he expects no reward or punishment.

3.explain: Lā yaḥuḍḍu: he doesn’t urge others to feed the miskīn, so surely he doesn’t feed him himself. The blame is for those able to help who hold back.
3.why: Reportedly about people who were stingy and excused themselves by saying: “Should we feed those whom Allah would feed if He wished?”

4.explain: Fa-wayl: so woe, destruction. It is for al-muṣallīn, people who do pray and are known for praying, but whose prayer is described next.

5.explain: ʿAn ṣalātihim sāhūn: careless about prayer itself, delaying it past its time, skipping its pillars, or not caring whether they pray. The Prophet ﷺ described it as wasting its time.

6.explain: Yurāʾūn: they pray and do good only to be seen, praying in public and leaving it when no one is watching.

7.explain: Al-māʿūn: small things people lend each other, like a bucket, pot or axe. Others say it means zakah. Refusing small things shows how tightly they hold on to everything else.
